narrative_before: In May 2024 Ascension, one of the largest US private healthcare systems, suffered a Black Basta ransomware attack after an employee accidentally downloaded a malicious file; the incident forced ambulance diversions, postponed appointments and reversion to manual/paper processes across many hospitals. Ascension later stated 7 of its ~25,000 servers were affected. While the initial access (malicious file download) is known and the Black Basta advisory AA24-131A gives generic TTPs (BITSAdmin/PsExec/RDP for lateral movement, Mimikatz for credentials), no public Ascension-specific source names an entry host and a lateral hop between identified internal hosts.
ambiguities: Entry (malicious file download on an employee workstation) is known, but no Ascension-specific named hosts or lateral hop were published; only generic Black Basta TTPs exist.
drop_reason: Entry point known (employee downloaded a malicious file) but no incident-specific lateral hop between identified hosts is publicly described. The BRIEF requires entry host AND one hop between identified hosts, so dropped.
